entities.summary: Sir Magdy Habib Yacoub is an Egyptian-British retired professor of cardiothoracic surgery at Imperial College London, best known for his early work in repairing heart valves with surgeon Donald Ross, adapting the Ross procedure, where the diseased aortic valve is replaced with the person's own pulmonary valve, devising the arterial switch operation (ASO) in transposition of the great arteries, and establishing the heart transplantation centre at Harefield Hospital in 1980 with a heart transplant for Derrick Morris, who at the time of his death was Europe's longest-surviving heart transplant recipient.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Yacoub's work on heart transplantation and the arterial switch operation has had a significant impact on European healthcare, with his centre at Harefield Hospital performing over 1,000 transplants and saving countless lives. His innovations have also paved the way for future advancements in cardiothoracic surgery.
